newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Sihanouk urges release of most Cambodia prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk urges release of most Cambodia prisoners.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk on Friday proposed the release of all but the most dangerous of the country's prisoners in the light of the pardons given to Khmer Rouge guerrillas.
The king, in a message released by the royal palace, also urged the government to demolish "the most revolting and ignominious prisons, starting with the sinister T-3".
Several high-profile prisoners, including journalists and politicians, have spent time in the dilapidated Phnom Penh prison built by French colonialists early this century.
Sihanouk said the nation's top monk, Tep Vong, had proposed he mark his 75th birthday on October 31 and Cambodia's independence day on November 9 by releasing as many prisoners as possible.

The king, who is empowered by the constitution to grant amnesty, said he backed the proposal and added that Tep Vong had told him co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen were favourable to the suggestion.

Sihanouk said that because the government had pardoned many Khmer Rouge guilty of countless serious crimes and welcomed many into the army, "I can no longer avoid giving liberty to all the male and female prisoners currently in our country's prisons, except for the most dangerous criminals".
"Whatever the crimes of these male and female prisoners... nobody can claim that these faults or crimes are as serious as those committed by the Khmer Rouge," he said.
Interior Ministry officials would not give a figure for prisoners held nationwide, but aid workers said the country's 23 prisons held an estimated 2,000 inmates.
They told Reuters this was a below-average prisoner-to-population ratio, but added that numbers were rising as the justice system improved, putting a strain on ancient facilities.
Cambodia has a population of 7.8 million, according to a 1988 estimate.
